title: The Greybeards - Masters of the Voice
content:
The Greybeards are an ancient and honored monastic order that dwells in their mountain sanctuary of High Hrothgar, located at the very peak of the Throat of the World. The monastery sits at the highest point in all of Skyrim and all of Tamriel.

Organization and Practice:
The Greybeards are masters of the Thu'um, or the Voice, which they use for the worship and glory of the gods rather than martial exploits. They live in absolute silence, speaking only through the use of the Thu'um itself. This vow of silence reflects their reverence for the power they wield and their commitment to the Way of the Voice philosophy.

Purpose and Role:
The Greybeards serve as teachers and guardians of the Thu'um. They summon those they deem worthy - particularly those who are Dragonborn - to High Hrothgar to test their Voice and train them in its proper use. The journey to reach them consists of the Seven Thousand Steps, a long pilgrimage up the mountainside.

History:
The order was founded by Jurgen Windcaller in the First Era, following the defeat of the dragons during the Dragon War. After witnessing the destruction caused by using the Voice as a weapon of war, Jurgen Windcaller meditated for years and established the Way of the Voice, teaching that the Thu'um should be used only for worship and meditation, not for conquest.

Leadership:
The Greybeards are led by Paarthurnax, an ancient dragon who sits at the very summit of the Throat of the World, above High Hrothgar itself. Paarthurnax betrayed Alduin during the Dragon War and taught mortals how to use the Thu'um, enabling them to defeat the dragons. He has meditated on the mountain for thousands of years.

Current Members:
The order consists of Master Arngeir (who serves as the speaker for the others), Borri, Einarth, and Wulfgar. Only Arngeir can speak in normal human language without causing destruction. The others communicate exclusively through the Thu'um.

title: The Thu'um - The Voice of the Dragons
content:
Nature of the Thu'um:
The Thu'um, also known as the Voice or Dragon Shouts, is a form of magic that uses the language of dragons to manifest powerful effects. Unlike traditional magic that manipulates the forces of nature, the Thu'um is the language of creation itself. When spoken properly, the words bend reality to match their meaning.

How It Works:
Each Shout consists of three Words of Power spoken in the dragon language (Dovahzul). The words can be used individually for lesser effects, or combined in sequence for full power. The Thu'um was originally used by dragons as their natural form of communication and as a weapon.

Learning the Thu'um:
For normal mortals, learning the Thu'um requires years or even decades of intense meditation and study. Each Word of Power must be meditated upon to understand its true meaning before it can be used. This is the method taught by the Greybeards through the Way of the Voice.

The Dragonborn Exception:
The Dragonborn possesses the dragon soul within a mortal body. This allows them to learn and use Shouts instinctively by absorbing the souls of slain dragons. They do not require years of meditation - they understand the Words of Power intuitively. This makes them uniquely powerful and potentially dangerous.

Common Shouts:
- Unrelenting Force (Fus Ro Dah): Projects a powerful force that staggers or throws targets
- Fire Breath (Yol Toor Shul): Breathes fire like a dragon
- Clear Skies (Lok Vah Koor): Clears away weather and magical effects
- Whirlwind Sprint (Wuld Nah Kest): Allows rapid forward movement
- Dragonrend (Joor Zah Frul): Forces dragons to land by making them mortal

Words of Power Locations:
Words of Power are inscribed on Word Walls throughout Skyrim. These walls were created by the ancient Nords to preserve the knowledge of the Thu'um. They are typically found in ancient Nordic ruins, dragon lairs, and sacred sites.

The Way of the Voice:
This philosophy, established by Jurgen Windcaller, teaches that the Thu'um is a gift from Kynareth and should be used only for worship and honor of the gods, not as a weapon. The Greybeards follow this philosophy strictly, though the Dragonborn is considered an exception by destiny.

title: High Hrothgar - Monastery of the Greybeards
content:
Location and Geography:
High Hrothgar is a monastery located at the peak of the Throat of the World, the highest mountain in Skyrim and in all of Tamriel. The mountain rises dramatically from the central tundra, its peak perpetually shrouded in snow and clouds.

The Seven Thousand Steps:
The journey to High Hrothgar consists of the Seven Thousand Steps, a pilgrimage path carved into the mountainside. Along this path are ten emblems with inscriptions that tell the story of the pilgrim's journey and the teachings of Jurgen Windcaller. The climb is treacherous, with harsh weather and dangerous wildlife.

The Monastery:
High Hrothgar itself is an ancient stone structure built in the traditional Nordic style. The interior is sparsely furnished, reflecting the Greybeards' ascetic lifestyle. The main hall features a circular floor pattern and is where the Greybeards conduct their meditations and teachings.

The Courtyard:
The monastery has an open courtyard where the Greybeards test those who have been summoned. It is here that they first demonstrate the power of the Thu'um by using Unrelenting Force to prove the visitor's worthiness.

The Summit:
Above High Hrothgar, at the very peak of the Throat of the World, is where Paarthurnax dwells. This area is only accessible after learning the Clear Skies Shout to dispel the magical blizzard that perpetually surrounds the summit. A Word Wall for the Dragonrend Shout is located here.

Historical Significance:
High Hrothgar has served as a place of pilgrimage and learning for thousands of years. It was here that Jurgen Windcaller established the Way of the Voice after his years of meditation. The monastery has remained largely unchanged since the First Era.

Access and Pilgrimage:
The path to High Hrothgar begins in Ivarstead, a small village at the base of the mountain. Pilgrims make the journey to seek wisdom, pay respects to the Greybeards, or answer a summons. Only those truly dedicated complete the entire climb.

Throat of the World - The Highest Peak:
The Throat of the World is not just a mountain but a sacred place in Nordic religion. It is said to be where the breath of Kynareth gave life to the first Nords. The mountain serves as a connection between the mortal world and the divine.

title: Paarthurnax - The Dragon of Wisdom
content:
Identity and Nature:
Paarthurnax is an ancient dragon who dwells at the summit of the Throat of the World, above High Hrothgar. He serves as the leader and master of the Greybeards, though he rarely interacts directly with mortals. His name means 'Ambition Overlord Cruelty' in the dragon language, a reminder of his dark past.

Dark History:
During the Dragon War in the Merethic Era, Paarthurnax was one of Alduin's most trusted lieutenants. He served as Alduin's right hand and committed terrible atrocities against mortals during the dragons' tyrannical rule. His past actions were brutal and unforgivable by many standards.

The Great Betrayal:
At some point during the Dragon War, Paarthurnax turned against Alduin. The reasons for this betrayal are complex - partly doubt in Alduin's rule, partly influenced by Kyne's intervention. He chose to aid mortals in their rebellion against dragon tyranny.

Teaching the Thu'um:
Paarthurnax's greatest contribution to mortals was teaching them how to use the Thu'um. Dragons speak the Thu'um naturally, but mortals had no knowledge of it. By teaching humans the Voice, Paarthurnax gave them the weapon they needed to defeat the dragons. This knowledge was taught to the ancient Nord heroes who would eventually found the Greybeards' order.

Redemption and Philosophy:
After the Dragon War, Paarthurnax retreated to the Throat of the World where he has meditated for thousands of years. He seeks to overcome his violent dragon nature through the Way of the Voice philosophy. He often speaks of the constant struggle between his nature and his choice, stating 'What is better - to be born good, or to overcome your evil nature through great effort?'

Personality and Wisdom:
Paarthurnax is philosophical and wise, often speaking in riddles and metaphors. He contemplates the nature of mortality, time, and violence. Despite his past, he is patient and serves as a mentor figure. He understands both the dragon and mortal perspectives uniquely.

Role with the Dragonborn:
When the Dragonborn reaches the summit, Paarthurnax serves as their teacher, instructing them in powerful Shouts and the philosophy behind them. He provides crucial information about Alduin and the dragon crisis. He helps the Dragonborn understand their nature and destiny.

The Blades' Judgment:
The Blades, ancient dragon slayers, demand Paarthurnax's death for his war crimes. They view his past atrocities as unforgivable, regardless of his subsequent redemption. This creates a moral dilemma for the Dragonborn.

title: Alduin - The World Eater
content:
Identity:
Alduin is the firstborn of Akatosh, the Dragon God of Time. In Nordic tradition, he is known as the World Eater, prophesied to consume the world at the end of time. He is the most powerful dragon in existence.

The Dragon War:
During the Merethic Era, Alduin ruled over Skyrim with absolute tyranny. He demanded worship and tribute from mortals, enforcing his rule through fear and violence. He commanded the Dragon Cult and other dragons, including Paarthurnax.

Banishment:
The ancient Nords, aided by Paarthurnax's teachings of the Thu'um, rebelled against Alduin. Unable to kill him, three heroes used an Elder Scroll to cast him forward through time. This occurred at the Throat of the World.

Return:
Alduin returns during the events of 4E 201, emerging from the time wound at the Throat of the World. However, instead of fulfilling his destiny to end the world, he seeks to reestablish dragon dominance over mortals.

Powers:
Alduin can resurrect other dragons by consuming their souls from ancient dragon burial mounds. He is immune to the Dragonrend Shout (until it is used against him) and possesses devastating Thu'um attacks. Only the Dragonborn can permanently kill him by absorbing his soul.

Final Battle:
The ultimate confrontation with Alduin takes place in Sovngarde, the Nordic afterlife. The Dragonborn must defeat him there with the aid of ancient heroes to save the world.

title: The Dragonborn - Dovahkiin
content:
Definition and Nature:
The Dragonborn, known as Dovahkiin in the dragon language, is a mortal blessed with the blood and soul of a dragon by Akatosh, the Dragon God of Time. This blessing is not hereditary but rather bestowed by divine will. A Dragonborn possesses a mortal body but contains the soul (Dov-Sil) of a dragon within.

Unique Abilities:
The primary ability of the Dragonborn is to permanently absorb the souls of slain dragons (Draconic vampirism). When a normal mortal kills a dragon, the dragon's soul remains intact and can be resurrected by Alduin. But when the Dragonborn kills a dragon, they absorb its soul, preventing any resurrection.

Instinctive Thu'um:
Unlike normal mortals who must meditate for years to understand a single Word of Power, the Dragonborn learns the Thu'um instinctively. They understand the meaning of Words of Power immediately upon seeing them inscribed on Word Walls. By absorbing dragon souls, they unlock the power to use these Words without years of training.

Historical Dragonborn:
Throughout history, there have been several known Dragonborn:
- Miraak: The First Dragonborn, who lived during the Merethic Era. He was a Dragon Priest who rebelled and was banished to Apocrypha by Hermaeus Mora.
- Alessia: The founder of the First Empire of Men, who bore the Amulet of Kings.
- Reman Cyrodiil: Founded the Second Empire and was a renowned warrior and conqueror.
- Tiber Septim (Talos): The most famous Dragonborn, who founded the Third Empire and achieved godhood. He conquered all of Tamriel and his Dynasty ruled until the Oblivion Crisis.
- The Last Dragonborn: Emerges in 4E 201 during the return of Alduin.

The Prophecy:
The Last Dragonborn is prophesied in the Prophecy of the Dragonborn, which foretells the return of dragons and the coming of one who will defeat Alduin:
'When misrule takes its place at the eight corners of the world
When the Brass Tower walks and Time is reshaped
When the thrice-blessed fail and the Red Tower trembles
When the Dragonborn Ruler loses his throne, and the White Tower falls
When the Snow Tower lies sundered, kingless, bleeding
The World-Eater wakes, and the Wheel turns upon the Last Dragonborn.'

Recognition:
The Greybeards can sense the presence of the Dragonborn through their use of the Thu'um. When the Dragonborn first absorbs a dragon soul, the Greybeards perform a traditional summoning by shouting the word 'Dovahkiin' from the Throat of the World, which can be heard across all of Skyrim.

Destiny and Purpose:
The Dragonborn's ultimate purpose is to defeat Alduin and save the world from destruction. However, their power also makes them dangerous - they possess the same potential for tyranny as the dragons themselves. The choice between using their power responsibly or for domination is theirs alone.

Relationship with Dragons:
The Dragonborn is both kin and bane to dragons. Dragons recognize them as Dovahkiin and often show respect even as enemies. Some dragons, like Paarthurnax, see the Dragonborn as proof that nature can be overcome by choice. Others, like Alduin, see them as an abomination - a mortal who dares to claim dragon power.

title: The Dragon War and the Way of the Voice
content:
The Merethic Era - Dragon Tyranny:
During the late Merethic Era, dragons ruled over mankind in Skyrim with absolute authority. Alduin, the World Eater, claimed dominion over mortals and demanded worship and tribute. The Dragon Cult, comprised of human Dragon Priests, enforced this tyranny and served as intermediaries between dragons and humans.

The Rebellion Begins:
Resistance began to form among the Nords who refused to submit to dragon rule. However, humans had no weapons that could effectively combat dragons. The war seemed hopeless until an unexpected ally emerged.

Paarthurnax's Betrayal:
Paarthurnax, one of Alduin's most trusted lieutenants, turned against his master and sided with mortals. His reasons were complex - philosophical doubts about Alduin's rulership and the intervention of Kyne (Kynareth), the goddess of storms and patron of mortals. Kyne sent Paarthurnax to teach humans the Thu'um.

Teaching the Thu'um to Mortals:
Paarthurnax taught selected humans how to use the Thu'um, the dragon language that could be wielded as a weapon. This was revolutionary - for the first time, humans had a tool that could match dragon power. The ancient Nord warriors trained extensively and became known as the 'Tongues' - masters of the Voice.

The War Intensifies:
With the power of the Thu'um, the tide of war began to turn. The Tongues became legendary warriors capable of fighting dragons on equal terms. Battles raged across Skyrim as more dragons fell to human Shouts. However, Alduin himself remained undefeatable.

The Banishment of Alduin:
Unable to kill Alduin, three legendary Nord heroes (Felldir the Old, Gormlaith Golden-Hilt, and Hakon One-Eye) used an Elder Scroll to cast Alduin forward through time. This occurred at the Throat of the World. With Alduin gone, the remaining dragons either fled, hid, or were hunted down. The Dragon Cult collapsed.

Post-War Period:
Following the Dragon War, the newly freed Nords established themselves as masters of their own fate. However, the power of the Thu'um proved to be a double-edged sword. The Tongues became arrogant and prideful, using their power for conquest and personal gain.

The War of Succession:
The abuse of the Thu'um led to a devastating civil war known as the War of Succession. Tongues used their Shouts against each other, causing massive destruction. The land of Skyrim was torn apart by warriors who treated the Voice as a tool of war rather than a sacred gift.

Jurgen Windcaller's Meditation:
A Tongue named Jurgen Windcaller was deeply affected by the destruction caused by the War of Succession. After a humiliating defeat at Red Mountain, he retreated into isolation and meditated for seven years on the proper use of the Thu'um.

Founding the Way of the Voice:
After his meditation, Jurgen Windcaller emerged with a new philosophy called the Way of the Voice. He taught that the Thu'um was a gift from Kynareth and should be used only for worship and honor of the gods, not as a weapon of war. Using the Voice for conquest or violence was a corruption of its sacred purpose.

Challenge at Skyrim's Throat:
Jurgen Windcaller challenged the seventeen strongest Tongues to a duel to prove his philosophy. The Tongues Shouted at him for days, but Jurgen Windcaller never raised his Voice in return. He demonstrated that true mastery of the Thu'um came from inner silence and discipline, not from violence.

Establishment of the Greybeards:
Convinced by his demonstration, the Tongues became Jurgen Windcaller's followers. They established the monastery of High Hrothgar at the peak of the Throat of the World and took vows of silence. They became the Greybeards, dedicating themselves to meditation and the proper understanding of the Voice.

Legacy:
The Way of the Voice became the accepted practice for the Thu'um in Skyrim. The Greybeards would continue this tradition for thousands of years, training worthy individuals while maintaining their isolation. Paarthurnax, who had enabled mortals to defeat the dragons, remained at the summit above High Hrothgar as the master of the order.

The Dragonborn Exception:
The Way of the Voice recognizes that the Dragonborn is an exception to their philosophy. Because Dragonborn are gifted the Thu'um by Akatosh himself for the specific purpose of combating dragons, they are permitted to use the Voice as a weapon. This is not a corruption but a fulfillment of their destiny.

title: Skyrim - The Land of the Nords
content:
Geography:
Skyrim is the northernmost province of Tamriel, a harsh land of mountains, forests, and tundra. The climate is cold and unforgiving, with long winters and heavy snowfall in many regions. The province is divided into nine holds, each governed by a Jarl.

Major Cities and Holds:
- Whiterun Hold: Central location, capital is Whiterun with its iconic Dragonsreach palace
- Solitude: Capital of Haafingar Hold and capital of all Skyrim, seat of the High King
- Windhelm: Ancient capital of Eastmarch Hold, city of Ysgramor
- Riften: Southern city in the Rift, known for the Thieves Guild
- Markarth: Western city built into a mountain, capital of the Reach
- Winterhold: Northern hold, home to the College of Winterhold
- Falkreath: Southern forested hold
- Morthal: Swampy hold in Hjaalmarch
- Dawnstar: Northern coastal hold, the Pale

The Throat of the World:
The highest mountain in all of Tamriel, sacred to the Nords. Home to High Hrothgar monastery and Paarthurnax. Site of many legendary events including the banishment of Alduin.

The Nords:
The inhabitants of Skyrim are primarily Nords, a race of tall, fair-haired humans known for their strength and resistance to cold. They value honor, courage in battle, and tradition. Nordic culture emphasizes warrior prowess and has a complex relationship with magic.

Religion:
The Nords traditionally worship the Nine Divines, though their interpretation differs from other provinces. Important deities include:
- Talos (Tiber Septim): Controversial worship due to the White-Gold Concordat
- Kynareth: Goddess of air and storms, giver of the Thu'um
- Shor: Nordic equivalent of Lorkhan, king of the gods
- Ysmir: Dragon of the North, associated with heroes and kings

The Civil War (4E 201):
Skyrim is embroiled in a civil war between:
- The Imperial Legion: Loyal to the Empire, enforcing the ban on Talos worship
- The Stormcloaks: Led by Ulfric Stormcloak, seeking independence for Skyrim

Historical Significance:
Skyrim has been the site of many pivotal events:
- The Dragon War in the Merethic Era
- Ysgramor's return and the founding of Nordic civilization
- The War of Succession and founding of the Way of the Voice
- The birthplace of Tiber Septim's empire
- The return of Alduin and the Last Dragonborn in 4E 201

title: The Companions
content:
The Companions are a group of elite warriors based in Jorrvaskr, the great mead hall in Whiterun. They are the oldest active organization in Skyrim, dating back to the return of Ysgramor from Atmora. The Companions take on contracts as mercenaries and protectors, priding themselves on their honor and martial prowess.

The Inner Circle:
The inner circle of the Companions, known as the Circle, are secretly werewolves, having accepted the beast blood from Aela the Huntress's lineage. This blessing/curse grants them enhanced combat abilities through transformation. The Companions follow a strict code of honor and avoid political entanglements, focusing on their reputation as warriors.

Notable Members:
- Kodlak Whitemane (Harbinger): The wise leader who seeks to cure the beast blood
- Aela the Huntress: Master archer and werewolf, member of the Circle
- Vilkas: Twin brother of Farkas, skilled warrior and member of the Circle
- Farkas: Twin brother of Vilkas, strong warrior and member of the Circle

History:
The organization accepts new members who prove their worth through combat and deeds. They trace their lineage back to Ysgramor's Five Hundred Companions who drove the elves from Skyrim.

title: College of Winterhold
content:
The College of Winterhold is the premier institution for magical study in Skyrim. Located in the northern city of Winterhold, the College stands isolated on a cliff after the Great Collapse destroyed most of the city in 4E 122.

Studies and Structure:
The College specializes in all schools of magic and houses the Arcanaeum, a library containing rare and powerful tomes. The College is led by the Arch-Mage and governed by a council of master wizards. Students at the College study various schools of magic including Destruction, Restoration, Alteration, Illusion, and Conjuration.

Relations with Winterhold:
The college has a strained relationship with Winterhold's citizens, who blame the mages for the Great Collapse. Despite this, the College continues its research and teaching.

Notable Members:
- Arch-Mage Savos Aren: Leader of the College
- Tolfdir: Elderly master wizard and teacher
- Faralda: Gatekeeper and Destruction expert
- J'zargo: Ambitious Khajiit student

Artifacts:
The College also possesses powerful artifacts including the Eye of Magnus, an ancient and mysterious source of immense magical power.

title: Dragon Language and Words of Power
content:
The dragon language, also called Dovahzul, is the ancient language spoken by dragons. It is inherently magical - when spoken, the words manifest their meaning into reality. This is the basis of the Thu'um.

Structure:
The language consists of words that can be combined into three-word Shouts. Each Word of Power is inscribed on Word Walls throughout Skyrim, hidden in ancient Nordic ruins and temples. These walls were created to preserve the knowledge of the Thu'um.

Common Words and Shouts:
- Fus (Force), Ro (Balance), Dah (Push) - Unrelenting Force
- Yol (Fire), Toor (Inferno), Shul (Sun) - Fire Breath
- Lok (Sky), Vah (Spring), Koor (Summer) - Clear Skies
- Wuld (Whirlwind), Nah (Fury), Kest (Tempest) - Whirlwind Sprint
- Joor (Mortal), Zah (Finite), Frul (Temporary) - Dragonrend

Learning:
The Dragonborn can learn these words by studying the walls and unlock their power by absorbing dragon souls. Dragons naturally speak this language, and when they fight, they are essentially debating with reality itself.

Philosophy:
Each word carries not just meaning but the concept itself. To truly understand a Word of Power is to understand its place in creation. This is why normal mortals must meditate for years on a single word.

title: Whiterun and Dragonsreach
content:
Whiterun is one of the major cities in Skyrim, located in the central tundra of the province. It serves as the capital of Whiterun Hold and is a major trading hub due to its central location.

City Districts:
The city is divided into three districts:
- Plains District: Lower level with shops, homes, and the main gate
- Wind District: Middle level with religious sites including the Temple of Kynareth
- Cloud District: Upper level with wealthy homes and Dragonsreach

Dragonsreach:
The jarl's palace sits at the highest point of the city. The palace was originally built to imprison a dragon named Numinex during the height of dragon rule. Its great hall features a massive dragon skull and can accommodate the capture of another dragon if needed. The palace's name literally means 'Dragon's Reach' commemorating this purpose.

Leadership:
Whiterun is ruled by Jarl Balgruuf the Greater, known for his wisdom and initial neutrality in the civil war. He is a fair and respected leader who prioritizes the safety of his people.

Jorrvaskr:
The city also houses Jorrvaskr, the ancient mead hall of the Companions warrior guild. This massive structure was built by Ysgramor's original companions and has stood for thousands of years.

Strategic Importance:
Whiterun's central location makes it strategically vital in Skyrim's conflicts. Control of Whiterun often means control of the province's trade routes and military movements.
